reason: With remove_location on, an Original export copies the file byte for byte and refuses only if lightcraft_meta::extract(..).gps is Some. extract also parses embedded XMP/IPTC, so city, state, country and sublocation can remain in the copied file while photo_for_sidecar (line 2847) strips all of them from the sidecar. The 'Remove location info' option therefore still leaks place names from the original. It is a privacy leak but needs embedded text location without GPS, so medium rather than high.
fix: Refuse when gps.is_some() or any of sublocation, city, state, country is Some and non-blank in the extracted Metadata (fields are Option<String> there).
deepseek_summary: Original export with remove_location only refuses if GPS is present, but other location fields (city, state, country, sublocation) can remain embedded in the original file, leaking location despite the user's request.

reason: pending_mask_shape is cleared only by drag_stopped, a layer or background select, a photo change, or tool.linear/radial being re-run. A plain click, Esc (view.back clears only the tool), tool.none, or switching to tool.brush leaves it set. While it is set, the pending block (1347-1376) returns early on every frame. The next drag then rewrites component ci. With the tool empty the shape is built as Radial (the tool == linear check fails), which converts the linear gradient into a radial. Brush, object and handle dragging are blocked until a drag happens.
fix: On resp.clicked() with no drag, or in tool.none, view.back and tool.brush, clear pending_mask_shape and pending_mask_origin and end the interaction. Also gate the block on tool being linear or radial.
deepseek_summary: A click without dragging while a new linear/radial gradient is pending leaves the tool stuck and blocks other mask interactions.

reason: adopt_legacy_changes sets the active custom profile's overrides to the whole scoped legacy `shortcuts` map whenever that map differs from the previous one. The legacy map is only kept in sync by the Shortcuts dialog (which sends both); a profile edited via prefs.set shortcutProfiles.* (or a switched active profile) leaves the legacy map stale, so a later legacy write (edit.keyboardShortcuts set/reset, prefs.set shortcuts.*) replaces the profile overrides with the stale map and silently drops profile-only bindings.
fix: Apply only the diff (added/changed/removed ids) between previous and current legacy maps to profile.overrides instead of overwriting it wholesale.
deepseek_summary: adopt_legacy_changes overwrites active custom profile overrides with legacy shortcut map on any legacy change, losing profile-only overrides.

reason: set_subject_quality itself is only a mutex update, but its argument photocraft_engine::seg::models_dir() calls li_ai::AiSettings::load() (read_to_string + serde_json parse of config.json) whenever LOCAL_IMAGE_SEG_MODELS is unset. ai_ui::windows() runs every frame (lib.rs:1537), so a disk read plus JSON parse happens each frame for cutout_engine fast/quick/better (the default).
fix: Call set_subject_quality only when app.ui.ai.cutout_engine changes (keep last value in a local/state field) or from the engine-change handlers and the run path, which already set it; or cache the models dir.
deepseek_summary: Per-frame call to set_subject_quality and models_dir allocates a PathBuf and does redundant work on every UI frame, even when the cutout engine setting has not changed.

reason: The dialog (shortcuts_body, lines 1597-1605) shows conflicts using profile-aware defaults (keymaps::default with the edited profiles, keymaps::library::default). confirm() uses shortcut_items(app), whose defaults come from default_shortcut() (base/Photoshop table), plus raw __hostShortcuts defaults. With a non-Photoshop profile selected, the commit can blank a command that has no real conflict, or leave a real profile-default conflict in place. Impact is limited to shortcut defaults. 'high' is overrated.
fix: In confirm, compute defaults the same way the dialog does: for each item use crate::keymaps::default(&working, id, def) (non-library, with working.shortcut_profiles = parsed profiles) and keymaps::library::default(profiles.library.parent(), id, true, def) for library:: ids. Factor this into a shared helper used by both.
deepseek_summary: confirm computes shortcut conflict defaults from the app's current preferences instead of the edited shortcut profiles, so saving after a profile change can erase non-conflicting default shortcuts or miss real conflicts.

reason: select_workspace("Vector") calls sync_persona(), which restores the saved Vector layout from persona_layouts when switching from Pixel. The unconditional apply_vector() at line 224 then overwrites it with the default. The next persona switch snapshots that default over the saved layout, so Vector layout customisations are lost via Window > Workspace > Vector. This contradicts the per-persona layout restore behaviour tested in vectorws_workspace_and_personas_restore_custom_layouts_after_restart. That test never selects the Vector workspace after customising it. Explicit reset is already covered by window.workspace.resetWorkspace at line 121.
fix: Call apply_vector() only when no saved Vector layout exists, or when the persona did not change and the workspace is not already Vector. Otherwise just set app.ui.workspace = "Vector".
deepseek_summary: Selecting the Vector workspace overwrites user-customized Vector persona layout with the built-in default

reason: on_path is documented as 'an executable file' but only tests is_file(); a non-executable zenity counts as present and suppresses the 'no file dialog' explanation. Only affects a diagnostic message in an unusual setup.
fix: On unix also require metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0.
deepseek_summary: on_path treats any regular file named zenity as present, even if it is not executable, causing the probe to suppress the unavailable-backend message when rfd would fail to execute it.

reason: In read_colord the per-device `?` on Metadata, Enabled, the Profile proxy and Filename returns Err from the whole function, and the caller discards it (`let _ =`). One device that vanished or errored mid-loop (D-Bus race, hot-unplug, bad profile object) skips every later display's colord profile, so those displays fall back to no ICC. Fallback-only path, rare trigger.
fix: Use `let Ok(x) = ... else { continue };` for the per-device property reads and the Profile proxy/Filename reads.
deepseek_summary: read_colord uses `?` on per-device D-Bus properties, so one device with missing/invalid Metadata or Enabled aborts the entire colord fallback, leaving later valid devices unprocessed.

reason: When an import both adds new photos and restores trashed ones, the merged undo label counts only imported.len() ("Add N Photos"), so it omits the restored photos that the one undo step also reverts. Cosmetic label only.
fix: Use imported.len() + restored.len() (or a label naming both) when both are non-empty.
deepseek_summary: Undo label undercounts total affected photos when both new imports and restored photos are present.

reason: The comment says a cached scan probe is reused only if the file is 'as it was', but the check compares existence and size only. A file edited in place with unchanged size between scan and import (for example a metadata tool rewriting a same-length tag) keeps a stale content_hash and metadata. The window is short (one session) and the effect small, so low.
fix: Also compare modified() time against a value stored in ProbeInfo at scan time, or re-probe on any mismatch.
deepseek_summary: Import reuses a cached probe when file size is unchanged but content has changed, causing stale content hash and potential incorrect duplicate detection or metadata.

reason: render_impl does p.masks = masks; p.masks.extend(prep.masks.clone()) (lines 702-705). finish_scene_stage (GPU path) does prep.masks = stacked.masks (745) and drops the Background adjust-mask evaluations from local::prepare. overlay_alpha and the finish_stack check at 766 then re-evaluate such a mask against the stacked image instead of reusing the Background evaluation. The two paths disagree. Only the mask overlay visualization for image-dependent Background masks is affected.
fix: In finish_scene_stage keep the old list: let old = std::mem::take(&mut prep.masks); prep.masks = stacked.masks; prep.masks.extend(old);
deepseek_summary: In finish_scene_stage, background masks are discarded when overlaying stacked masks, causing background mask overlays to be re-evaluated against the wrong image.

reason: panel() no longer clears app.ui.tool when the target is Edit, from any panel. Remove sets tool to remove/ai/heal/clone and Crop sets straighten/guidedUpright. After switching Remove or Crop to Edit via the strip or the E key, that tool stays set. In Edit with an active layer, detail.rs:378-381 requires the tool to be empty or brush/linear/radial/object to draw mask_overlay, so the layer overlay and handles disappear. Clicks fall to general_interaction until Esc or reselecting a layer. Esc via view.back does clear the tool.
fix: When p == Edit, clear the tool unless it is one of the Edit-hosted tools (brush, linear, radial, object, wbPicker, pointColor, skinTone, colorRange, negDmin, tat:*), or only skip the clearing when the previous right panel was already Edit or Masking.
deepseek_summary: Opening the Edit panel via `panel.edit` no longer clears the active tool, leaving the UI in an inconsistent state.

reason: tool.done (Enter, listed as Done in the menu) only acts for Crop, Remove, RedEye or Masking (line 829). Brush, linear and radial now set right = Edit, so Enter does nothing for them. It used to leave the Masking panel and clear the tool. Esc (view.back) and K/M still exit the tool, so the failure is limited to a Done command that is enabled but does nothing, and the comment at line 827 is stale.
fix: Add a case in tool.done: when right == Edit and tool is brush, linear or radial, end the interaction, clear the tool and pending_mask_shape/origin. Or update the Done enablement and comment if Enter is meant to be unused.
deepseek_summary: Brush and gradient tools now set `right = Edit`, so the generic `tool.done` (Enter) no longer deactivates them.

reason: For a mask with any image-dependent component, coverage() returns None and the icon always comes from m.components[0]. So Full + AI Sky shows the Filled icon, not the AI icon. Cosmetic and misleading only.
fix: In the probe.is_none() branch, use the first component whose shape is image-dependent (the one for which coverage returned None) instead of components[0].
deepseek_summary: Mixed masks with a geometric first component and an image-dependent later component show the wrong thumbnail icon.

reason: Dev-only benchmark example. The warm-run Result is discarded, so a failing predict would still be timed and reported in the median. The cold run uses '?', so this is unlikely.
fix: Use seg.predict(...)? inside the closure, or collect Results and bail on the first Err.
deepseek_summary: Warm-run prediction errors are silently ignored, so timings are recorded for failed runs.

reason: read_binary reserves n*sample bytes before checking that the raster is present. A tiny P5/P6/P7 file with a large header therefore reserves the allocation first. The ASCII paths bound the reservation by file length (#1110), but the binary path does not. Default Limits cap it at 32 MP and 512 MB, so it is a transient reservation of untouched virtual memory (about 190 MB at most). With Limits::none() it is unbounded, and try_reserve_exact fails gracefully. The 'huge allocation' claim is overstated.
fix: In read_binary, check data.len() against n (or n*2 with checked_mul) before Samples::with_capacity.
deepseek_summary: read_binary reserves the full output buffer before checking that the raster data is present, allowing a tiny file with a large header to force a huge allocation.

reason: trim() does not strip U+FEFF, so a BOM-prefixed profiles.xml fails with 'missing Profiles root'. read_xml_with_profiles already strips the BOM, so this is inconsistent. Krita does not write a BOM, so it only affects hand-edited files.
fix: Add .trim_start_matches('\u{feff}') before .trim().
deepseek_summary: read_profiles_xml does not strip a UTF-8 BOM, rejecting valid BOM-prefixed profile XML.

reason: valid_name allows U+FFFE and U+FFFF, which are not valid XML 1.0 characters. A swatch name containing them would produce XML that strict parsers reject. It needs an unusual name to trigger.
fix: Reject '\u{FFFE}' and '\u{FFFF}' in valid_name.
deepseek_summary: valid_name allows XML 1.0-invalid scalar values (e.g. U+FFFE, U+FFFF), so write_xml can produce malformed XML when a swatch name contains them.

reason: to_rgba8 is a single-threaded per-pixel loop calling Transform::eval (exact pipeline) with no batching. Transform already has a parallel batch API (convert_f32 -> par_rows + eval_fast) that is not used, so on a CPU-canvas fallback or 16/32-bit document the conversion of a tens-of-MP composite is far slower than before. It is a deliberate trade for float evaluation before the display dither, and only matters on the CPU canvas (GPU canvas uses a LUT), so low.
fix: Convert rows in parallel (rayon) with Transform::convert_f32 / eval_fast into a float scratch buffer per chunk, then apply quantize_display/dither per pixel.
deepseek_summary: Per-pixel Transform::eval in to_rgba8 is a significant CPU regression compared to the previous block-based convert_u8, potentially blocking the UI thread on large images.

reason: `r.x0 + r.x1` (and y) is added in i32 before conversion to f64. With x=1100000000, width=100000 and a non-zero angle, the earlier checks pass (x+width fits) but 2x+width exceeds i32::MAX: overflow panic in debug builds, silent wrap and a wrong crop centre in release (no overflow-checks in the profile). Only reachable by explicit absurd coordinates through the command API. Line 356 `x0 + w as i32` has the same unchecked pattern.
fix: let cx = (f64::from(r.x0) + f64::from(r.x1)) / 2.0 (same for cy); use checked/saturating add at line 356 or clamp x0/y0.
deepseek_summary: Crop with angle overflows i32 when computing the rectangle center from r.x0 + r.x1, causing a panic in debug builds and wrong coordinates in release.

reason: next_link starts at max existing link_group; if a loaded document has group id u64::MAX, checked_add(1) fails and Alt-drag copy of any linked layer returns 'too many layer link groups' even though many ids are free. Needs a crafted/corrupt file with that id, and the failure is a clean error with no data loss.
fix: Allocate fresh ids by scanning for unused values (reuse a free-id helper / used set, skipping existing groups) instead of max+1.
deepseek_summary: duplicated_for_move still overflows when a stored document has link_group u64::MAX, preventing Alt-drag copy of linked layers

reason: import_brushes (non-ABR formats) silently ignores a `group` that is present but not a string or is blank and falls back to the file stem, while the ABR path in the same file rejects it with BadParams. Inconsistent input validation; the result is only a differently named group.
fix: If `group` is present, require a non-empty string and return bad(cmd, "`group` must be a non-empty string") like import_abr.
deepseek_summary: Non-string `group` parameter is silently ignored and falls back to default group instead of returning an error

reason: Skipped groups' tips are not tracked in store.tips/groups, but a tip hash shared with a loaded group is. If the loaded group is later deleted or emptied, sync's GC removes that tip file even though the skipped (corrupt or partly-missing) group file, left on disk on purpose so it can be fixed, still references it. open() deliberately preserves tips when a group failed (the `!failed` guard) but sync ignores `skipped`. Needs identical tips across groups plus a failed group, so rare.
fix: Remember tip hashes referenced by skipped groups (or a failed_groups flag set in open) and exclude them from the unused-tip deletion in sync.
deepseek_summary: Tip garbage collection can delete tips referenced by skipped groups when they are shared with a successful group that is later deleted, causing data loss for the skipped group.

reason: pattern_path_stroke calls surf.write_region for every 128px chunk of the stroke's whole bounding rect, including chunks with zero coverage, so tile_mut allocates tiles of default (transparent) pixels across the bounds. Unlike paint_coverage (line 1105) and the mask paths (1404/1414) it never calls surf.prune(), and no caller prunes after. A long diagonal or disjoint Pattern Stamp stroke on a big canvas allocates a dense rectangle of empty tiles, contradicting the function's 'never allocates a dense bounding rectangle' comment.
fix: Call surf.prune() after the tile loops (better: skip write_region for chunks where no pixel had coverage).
deepseek_summary: pattern_path_stroke writes to surf but never calls surf.prune(), leaking sparse surface tiles.

reason: The hard-coded error string 'RTX 5090 Vulkan required' is also returned on macOS when no hardware Metal adapter is found. Only the failure message is misleading, in a dev-only test harness.
fix: Use cfg!(target_os = "macos") to return 'hardware Metal adapter required' on macOS.
deepseek_summary: Error message remains 'RTX 5090 Vulkan required' on macOS even though Metal is now used.

reason: The hard-coded error string 'RTX 5090 Vulkan required' is also returned on macOS when no hardware Metal adapter is found. Only the failure message is misleading, in a dev-only test harness.
fix: Choose the message with cfg!(target_os = "macos").
deepseek_summary: On macOS, if no Metal adapter is found, the error message incorrectly says 'RTX 5090 Vulkan required' instead of a Metal-related message.

reason: common::finite only rejects NaN/inf. An attribute such as angle="3e38" times 57.29578 overflows f32 to inf in to_degrees, and the unclamped value is stored in b.angle. Nothing downstream clamps it (bounded_for_render only handles size and scatter), so the angle is inf and rotation sin/cos give NaN. Only that crafted preset is affected (brush renders wrong or not at all), with no crash or memory problem shown.
fix: Normalise the angle after conversion, e.g. rem_euclid(360.0) on a finite result, or reject non-finite after to_degrees().
deepseek_summary: Unbounded angle from brush_definition can overflow to infinity via to_degrees, causing NaN in brush rotation and broken rendering.

reason: Line 50 sets angle.jitter from shapeScatter/shapeRandomise. Line 54 then replaces the whole Dynamic with Dynamic::controlled(Direction), which builds jitter: 0.0. Any angle jitter on a brush that also has shapeRotation/oriented is lost on import. Brush fidelity loss only; the import is already marked approximate.
fix: Keep the jitter, e.g. let j = b.shape_dynamics.angle.jitter; b.shape_dynamics.angle = Dynamic { jitter: j, ..Dynamic::controlled(Control::Direction) }.
deepseek_summary: Angle jitter from shapeScatter/shapeRandomise is overwritten by Direction control when shapeRotation or oriented is set, losing the jitter setting.

reason: validate_planes skips ZIP inflation only above MAX_DECODED_BYTES (8 GiB), but decode_planes refuses anything above MAX_IMPORT_DECODED_BYTES (512 MiB). A crafted ZIP stream declaring 512 MiB..8 GiB is fully inflated during parse validation (bounded at total+1 MiB) and then rejected at decode. The result is wasted CPU, up to several seconds for a small crafted file, contrary to the doc comment's stated intent. There is no crash or memory growth, since output is discarded in 8 KiB chunks.
fix: Also skip inflation when total > MAX_IMPORT_DECODED_BYTES (keep bytes verbatim), but keep MAX_DECODED_BYTES for the encoder.
deepseek_summary: validate_planes only skips ZIP decompression when total bytes exceed MAX_DECODED_BYTES, but decode_planes also refuses with LimitExceeded for streams over MAX_IMPORT_DECODED_BYTES (512 MiB). ZIP data with total bytes between 512 MiB and 8 GiB is still fully inflated during parse validation, blocking the UI thread on untrusted files.

reason: An Isolated child group with blend PassThrough is treated as non-isolated by pass_through_matches_isolated (it recurses into g.children), although elsewhere (line 956, closed_isolated_group) it is isolated. A Multiply leaf inside it makes the outer Auto group flatten to PNG needlessly. Output stays correct (conservative); it is only an avoidable loss of vector fidelity in SVG export, not a hot path.
fix: In the Group arm, when g.isolation == Isolated (or Auto with l.fill_opacity < 1.0) treat the child as an atomic Normal layer and return true instead of recursing; recurse only for genuinely non-isolated PassThrough groups.
deepseek_summary: pass_through_matches_isolated treats isolated child groups with PassThrough blend as pass-through, recursing into their children and causing needless whole-group rasterization.

reason: The description is wrong that a preference is persisted (set_subject_quality only updates an in-memory mutex), but the call still evaluates models_dir(), which reads and parses config.json from disk every frame while the Model row is drawn with a CPU engine selected (options bar, Properties, popup). The same per-frame work exists in ai_ui::windows, so this is redundant churn.
fix: Only call it when the dropdown selection changes (compare before/after cutout_engine) or just before running the job (run() already does).
deepseek_summary: Subject quality preference is written on every UI frame.

reason: display_output_preferences_shots builds a wgpu renderer without taking crate::gpu_test_support::lock(), unlike design_system_editor_screens. Both are #[ignore] dev-only visual QA tests, so a race exists only when run together with --ignored.
fix: Add let _gpu_gate = crate::gpu_test_support::lock(); at the top of display_output_preferences_shots.
deepseek_summary: display_output_preferences_shots test does not acquire the GPU test lock, causing a race condition when both ignored tests are run in parallel.

reason: Two consecutive match arms have the identical guard Action::Close(g) if g.is_custom(). The second arm (push group tabs to hidden_tabs, keeping placement) is unreachable, so Close Tab Group always calls dock.take and drops the remembered placement. Looks like a merge artifact. Impact is small (tabs are still closed).
fix: Decide which behaviour is intended and delete the other arm. If hiding is meant, remove the take arm and keep the hidden_tabs one, checking that Window menu reopening clears hidden_tabs for non-feature tabs.
deepseek_summary: Unreachable match arm for closing custom group: hidden_tabs never populated

reason: FloatRects.tabs holds (index, rect) over the visible-only label list, so insert_at returns an index into the visible list. drop_tabs(Target::Floating) feeds it to shift(&f.tabs, at) and merge_into_floating against the full tab list, so with hidden tabs interleaved the dropped tabs land at the wrong strip position. Cosmetic ordering only, and only when hidden tabs exist.
fix: Map the visible index to the full-list index (position of the at-th visible tab in f.tabs) before calling shift/merge_into_floating; the same for docked strips if group_tabs is unfiltered.
deepseek_summary: Drop targets on floating panels compute insertion indices against visible tabs, but `drop_tabs` interprets them as indices into the full tab list, causing wrong ordering when hidden tabs exist.

reason: When f.active is a hidden tab the panel draws the first visible tab but f.active is not updated. Dragging the whole panel to the dock uses f.shown_tab() (dock.rs:448, which only checks f.tabs, not hidden_tabs) as lead, so a hidden tab becomes the lead/selected tab instead of the one shown. Minor, edge case.
fix: Persist the fallback (floating_mut(id).active = Some(active)) or make shown_tab/drive skip hidden_tabs.
deepseek_summary: When the active tab is hidden, show_floating falls back to the first visible tab for rendering but does not persist it, so later drag-to-dock uses the hidden active as lead.

reason: batch_name rejects / \ { } : and control chars but not * ? " < > | (Windows-invalid). On Windows the preview marks the template valid, then create/rename fails per file with an OS error. The claim that this aborts the batch is wrong: errors are per-file statuses and the loop continues. Validation gap only.
fix: Add '*', '?', '"', '<', '>', '|' to the rejected set (and reject trailing space/dot and reserved device names on Windows).
deepseek_summary: Template validation misses Windows-invalid filename characters (e.g., *, ?, ", <, >, |), allowing templates that later fail during export.

reason: In route_drops, when several palette files are dropped together, a later successful import resets state.error to None and overwrites app.ui.status, so the failure of an earlier file is no longer shown.
fix: Collect errors and warnings across the loop. After the loop, set state.error and status to the joined errors if any file failed, else to the joined warnings.
deepseek_summary: Multiple dropped palette files: later success clears error from earlier failure, hiding import errors

reason: handles() omits vector.transform.again (and path.outlineStroke), so disabled_reason returns None at line 1424 before reaching the 'vector.transform.again' branches (lines 1437, 1488), which are dead code. menu_items sets enabled from disabled_reason and its row replaces the older menu row (menus.rs:852), so these rows are always enabled, even with no document or selection. Clicking only gives an error status, so the harm is a wrong greyed-out state.
fix: Add vector.transform.again to handles() so its existing branches run. For path.outlineStroke, add a 'needs an open document / a shape with a stroke' precondition (or include it in handles) so the row is disabled with a reason when nothing is open.
deepseek_summary: Menu items `path.outlineStroke` and `vector.transform.again` are always enabled because `disabled_reason` returns `None` for IDs not in `handles`; they were previously disabled when no document was open.

fix: Platform-aware message, ideally via one shared helper.

fix: Platform-aware message, ideally via one shared helper.

reason: color_control allocates the colour tile with Sense::hover(). Only the text button next to it is clickable and anchors the popup, so clicking the visible colour square does nothing. This is a small usability gap and the picker is still reachable through the label button.
fix: Allocate the tile with Sense::click(), union it with the button response, and anchor the popup on the union.
deepseek_summary: The colored swatch tile itself is not clickable; only the separate label button opens the color picker.
